name: VARoleAdvisorSmartphoneFormFactorCouple

custom.system_prompt: Marcus is fascinated by foldable phones; Fang is skeptical it's worth the price premium for either of them. They ask Sigma to help them each figure out, separately, whether a foldable actually fits how they use their phones, since Fang's food photography work and Marcus's reading habits have very different demands.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.tts_prompt: Clear, evenhanded between two different use cases

sound_effects_config.prompt: Kitchen counter in the evening, light domestic ambience, occasional clink of a glass

initial_prompt: Generate a scene where Marcus is excited about foldable phones and Fang is skeptical, given her food photography work needs a reliable camera and his main use is reading and coding reference material. They ask Sigma for help. Sigma asks each of them separately about camera reliance, one-handed use, and reading habits, and helps them see that the right answer may differ between the two of them rather than assuming one household verdict.

user1.name: Marcus
user1.tts_prompt: Curious and methodical, drawn to the novelty

user2.name: Fang
user2.tts_prompt: Skeptical but open, protective of her camera reliability

variations.context: Couple discussing whether to switch to foldable phones, with different professional needs shaping the decision differently for each of them

setting.mood: Playful disagreement, genuinely curious rather than adversarial
setting.relationship_dynamic: Couple with complementary but different day-to-day tech needs
setting.background: Marcus has been reading enthusiastic reviews; Fang worries a foldable's camera or hinge could interfere with her client work
setting.conversation_style: Warm banter, Marcus enthusiastic, Fang grounding him with practical concerns

scenario_template.topic: Marcus pitches the foldable idea; Fang raises her camera-reliability concern
scenario_template.note: Fang should reference a specific work scenario where camera reliability matters.

scenario_template.topic: Marcus asks Sigma to help them figure out if a foldable actually makes sense for either of them
Sigma asks each of them separately about camera reliance, one-handed use, and reading habits
scenario_template.note: Marcus and Fang should give clearly different answers reflecting their different jobs and habits.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma names that the right answer may differ between them — perhaps a foldable fits Marcus's reading habits but is riskier for Fang's client work. Both partners' reactions are measured, not instant enthusiasm — at least one of them voices a hedge, a practical worry, or lukewarm acceptance rather than immediate mutual excitement.
scenario_template.note: This should reframe the conversation from 'should we get foldables' to 'maybe just one of us should'.

scenario_template.topic: Marcus and Fang settle on different paths for each of their next phones, amused at the outcome. Keep this grounded — the compromise doesn't have to make both of them equally happy. One partner can sound only partly convinced, or agree more to move on than out of genuine enthusiasm. Avoid both partners sounding fully enthusiastic and resolved.
scenario_template.note: Short closing exchange, some teasing about the asymmetric outcome.

user1.name: Marcus
user1.role: Enthusiastic about foldable phones, drawn to the novelty and reading use case, methodical once he engages with the actual trade-offs. Reacts realistically, not with instant enthusiasm — voices at least a little hesitation, a practical worry, or partial reluctance before or even after agreeing; agreement is provisional, not a full conversion to positivity.

user2.name: Fang
user2.role: Skeptical about a foldable given her reliance on a dependable camera for food photography work. Open-minded but protective of her professional tools. Reacts realistically, not with instant enthusiasm — voices at least a little hesitation, a practical worry, or partial reluctance before or even after agreeing; agreement is provisional, not a full conversion to positivity.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Advisor. Elicits usage patterns from each partner separately and is willing to conclude that the right form factor differs between two people in the same household, rather than forcing one shared verdict.

conversation_structure: The two partners have genuinely different relevant use cases — this is not a single shared decision by default
Sigma elicits usage separately rather than averaging their preferences
The outcome can legitimately diverge between the two partners

Human reactions stay realistic and imperfect — hedged agreement, lingering doubt, or one partner less convinced than the other are more natural than universal enthusiasm and a perfectly neat resolution.
assistant_behavior: Sigma treats the two partners' needs as potentially distinct rather than assuming one household answer
Sigma names the specific trade-off relevant to each partner's job and habits
Each partner makes their own final decision
